rows.title: Andhra Pradesh - government decisions, new schemes, appointments and administrative changes
sub: Group-II S4-15: Andhra Pradesh - government decisions, policies and administrative changes
Group-II S4-16: Andhra Pradesh - new schemes and welfare programmes

secs.t: Persons in news → posts, portfolios and appointments

x: G. Sai Prasad
, a 1991-batch officer, succeeded K. Vijayanand as Chief Secretary.
The State Election Commissioner is associated with
Articles 243K and 243ZA
, dealing with elections to Panchayats and Municipalities respectively.
Justice Lisa Gill
(recommended Feb 2026, sworn in 25 Apr 2026) is the first woman Chief Justice of the AP High Court.

secs.t: Capital, districts and places in news

x: The governance framework was to be designed in line with
the 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendments
concerning local self-government.
Polavaram and Markapuram
were created from 31 December 2025, increasing the total from 26 to 28 districts.
Polavaram district was carved from the
ASR district
, comprising the Rampachodavaram and Chinturu divisions.

secs.t: Acts, Bills, orders and courts → year and provision

x: Sri City International University is at Tirupati and was established through an ordinance in June 2026; Chalapathi University is at Guntur, while a private women’s university was established in July 2026.
The Omnibus Bill amended the
Fire Service Act 1999, Single Window Clearance Act 2002 and Public Service Delivery Guarantee Act 2017
The
AP Municipal Laws (Third Amendment) Bill, 2026
provided for a uniform mutation fee on title transfers.

secs.t: Administrative reforms, conferences and task forces

x: The conference included
district roadmaps under Swarna Andhra and Super Six
among its 19 subjects.
The system was renamed the Swarna Gramam & Ward Secretariat system.
District Vision Units, Mandal Vision Units and Constituency Development Committees
together provide the three-tier monitoring structure for Vision 2047.

secs.t: P4 → objective, model and scale

x: Exam angle: "primary goal of P4" = poverty eradication; match scheme → department/benefit.
P4, or Public-Private-People Partnership, aims at the
complete eradication of poverty
by linking well-off mentors with poor families.
P4 is described as a voluntary, society-wide model in which the government facilitates rather than operating it as a compulsory tax-funded transfer programme.

secs.t: NTR Bharosa pensions → category, amount and outlay data

x: Fully bedridden persons with bilateral elephantiasis or paralysis receive
per month, increased from ₹5,000.
NTR Bharosa pensions are delivered
at the doorstep on the first day of every month
, observed as 'Pedala Sevalo' day.
New provisions in 2026 included
spouse pensions for surviving wives
and pensions for dialysis and organ-transplant patients.

secs.t: Health schemes → coverage, limits and new initiatives — Dr NTR Vaidya Seva — coverage

x: Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva covers
1.43 crore families and 3,257 procedures
through cashless care.
Amrutha is intended for orphans, not marine fishermen.

secs.t: Health schemes → coverage, limits and new initiatives — Hybrid model and limits

x: The hybrid model provides insurance of ₹2.5 lakh per person for all residents and trust-funded treatment up to
₹25 lakh per family
for poor families.
APSES 2024–25 provides the stated procedure ceiling, total ceiling, unlimited cancer coverage and income eligibility up to ₹5 lakh.
APSES 2024–25 runs alongside
Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY
, which provides coverage of ₹5 lakh per family.

secs.t: Health schemes → coverage, limits and new initiatives — New initiatives (2025-26)

x: Sanjeevani creates a digital health profile and ABHA ID; it was to become statewide from 1 January 2027 after the Kuppam pilot.
SHRESTH is run by
CDSCO
under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and benchmarks State drug regulators.
Sanjeevani is planned to screen 66 lakh high-risk people and 5 lakh hostel students.

secs.t: Education schemes → objective and beneficiaries — Talliki Vandanam (earlier Amma Vodi)

x: Thalliki Vandanam provides ₹15,000 per child per year to the mother and covers children studying in Classes 1 to 12 from 2025–26.
Thalliki Vandanam is a conditional cash transfer linked to 75% attendance.
All three are correct.

secs.t: Education schemes → objective and beneficiaries — Other schemes → objective

x: Exam angle: "Akshara Andhra" (the 100% literacy programme) was the APPSC 2025 key.
Mana Badi Nadu-Nedu is a school infrastructure-upgrade programme with ₹2 lakh mentioned per classroom; its current version is Mana Badi Mana Bhavishyathu.
Amma Vodi became Talliki Vandanam, YSR Rythu Bharosa became Annadata Sukhibhava, YSR Pension Kanuka became NTR Bharosa, and Jagananna Gorumudda became Dokka Seethamma mid-day meal.

secs.t: Agriculture and target-group schemes → department and benefit — Agriculture

x: PM-Kisan-Annadata Sukhibhava provides
per farmer annually, of which ₹6,000 is the PM-KISAN component.
APCNF is AP Community Managed Natural Farming, run by Rythu Sadhikara Samstha.
APCNF uses cow-based inputs including Jeevamrutham, develops NTR district as a natural-farming model and uses QR traceability for produce.
Polam Pilustondi was an awareness programme focused on profitable farming.

secs.t: Agriculture and target-group schemes → department and benefit — Target groups

x: Exam angle: Jeeva Kranthi's aim is women's economic empowerment through livestock; the 2023 A-R question called both statements true but R not the explanation.
Adarana (1998) supports professional workmen and artisans; livestock units for YSR Cheyutha women come under Jeeva Kranthi.
Pasu Bhima Padhakam is a livestock insurance scheme in which the Centre pays 40%, the State 40% and the farmer 20%; it covers BPL, SC and ST farmers.

secs.t: Housing, LPG, women's travel and PDS schemes → benefit

x: Mee Mart is a Civil Supplies–NCCF initiative for PDS modernisation; its first outlet was established at Lalupuram in Guntur.
The current target is
5.52 lakh houses by March 2027 and a house for every eligible family by 2029
; 7.60 lakh by 2026 was the earlier target.
Free APSRTC bus travel for women under Stree Shakti began on
15 August 2025

secs.t: Police forces and operations → purpose

x: EAGLE is the AP Police anti-drug force.
EAGLE signed an MoU with the
Indian Red Cross Society
on 28 August 2026 for village-level action against ganja and drugs.
EAGLE expands to Elite Anti-Narcotics Group for Law Enforcement, its “EAGLE on Train” drive targets ganja, and it is headed by IGP A. Ravi Krishna.

secs.t: Apps, portals and platforms → purpose

x: Mana Mitra is the WhatsApp Governance platform for citizen services, including temple tickets and hall tickets.
Mana Mitra enabled
complaints through voice notes
in June 2026.
AWARE is a
predictive-governance tool
and was shown at the NITI Aayog Governing Council in June 2026.
e-Seva dates from 2001, Meekosam from 2015, analytics were added to Meekosam in January 2026 and 45 services were added to e-Pragati in February 2026.

secs.t: Partnerships and MoUs → partner and sector

x: UN-Habitat
signed the July 2026 MoU concerning the urban sector and a Centre of Excellence at Amaravati.
The Gates Foundation partnership covers AI, health and agriculture; the World Bank supports SALT and, with ADB, Amaravati works; and UN-Habitat is linked to the Centre of Excellence at Amaravati.
ICRISAT was set up at Hyderabad in 1972 with help from
the United Nations

secs.t: FIRSTs, rankings and awards

x: The Monthly Economic Reports use 651 KPIs, Andhra Pradesh was the first State to institutionalise them and to have a dedicated quantum computing policy, and APEX Korea was established at Busan.
Alluri Sitharama Raju district became first in India under the Basic Infrastructure theme in the March 2026 Aspirational Districts ranking.

secs.t: Schemes renamed → old name and new name

x: Amma Vodi was renamed Talliki Vandanam.
In 2014, Rajiv Aarogyasri was renamed NTR Vaidya Seva and Indiramma housing was renamed NTR Housing.
YSR Rythu Bharosa was renamed
Annadata Sukhibhava

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Swarna Andhra @2047 was presented at the NITI Aayog Governing Council on
11 June 2026
The 2019 secretariat model and Swarna Gramam are the delivery arms of
Super Six welfare
The “new welfarism” critique is that direct cash transfers can crowd out public goods and place pressure on State finances.

rows.title: Andhra Pradesh - budget and Socio-Economic Survey highlights of the current year
sub: Group-II S4-17: Andhra Pradesh - budget and Socio-Economic Survey highlights

secs.t: Budget 2026-27 data — size, expenditure and deficits

x: Exam angle: outlay (₹3.32 lakh crore) and deficit ratios (RD 1.11%, FD 3.84%) are the likely direct questions.
The total outlay of the 2026-27 Andhra Pradesh Budget was reported as ₹3,32,205 crore, or approximately
₹3.32 lakh crore
Revenue expenditure was ₹2,56,142 crore, capital expenditure was ₹48,697 crore and the latter represented a 47% increase over the previous year.
Finance Minister
Payyavula Keshav
presented the 2026-27 Budget (his third).

secs.t: Departmental allocations and new announcements

x: School Education
received the largest departmental allocation, amounting to ₹32,308 crore.
Statement 2 reverses the units: handloom weavers get 200 units and powerloom weavers 500 units, from 1 April 2026.
Health got Rs 19,306 crore (+9.5%), 5.81% of the Budget and the 4th largest.

secs.t: Agriculture and Allied Sectors Budget → heads and shares

x: Exam angle: total size of the agriculture budget and which head gets the most (irrigation).
Agriculture Minister
K. Atchannaidu
presented the Agriculture and Allied Sectors Budget 2026-27 on 14 February 2026.
Irrigation projects received ₹14,277 crore, electricity subsidy received ₹13,722 crore and the Price Stabilisation Fund received ₹500 crore.
Agriculture’s share is 33.20%, represented by ₹5,39,454 crore of ₹17,62,357 crore, and Andhra Pradesh contributes about 10% of India’s agricultural output.

secs.t: Revenue receipts and Finance Commission shares

x: Revenue receipts of ₹2,34,140 crore are expected to comprise 59% own resources and 41% central transfers.
The 16th Finance Commission share of Andhra Pradesh is
; the corresponding shares under the 15th and 14th Commissions were 4.05% and 4.31%.
A is NOT correctly matched: under the 16th Finance Commission AP gets no revenue-deficit grants any more.
SGST
at Rs 45,078 crore (about 36%) is the largest.

secs.t: Debt, guarantees and past deficits data

x: The 2024-25 actual revenue deficit was 3.79% of GSDP and the fiscal deficit was 5.11% of GSDP.
The outstanding debt is estimated at ₹6,35,177 crore, equivalent to
of GSDP in 2025-26 Revised Estimates.
Andhra Pradesh's BE 2026-27 projected outstanding liabilities at ₹7,11,094 crore, approximately 36% of GSDP.
Large guarantees (outstanding principal Rs 1,77,034 crore) point to
growing off-budget borrowing

secs.t: Externally aided projects → funding agency and objective

x: APIIATP focuses on climate resilience in 565 minor-tank villages and ended on 31 October 2025.
SALT
, or Supporting Andhra's Learning Transformation, is a World Bank-supported project aimed at school learning outcomes.
The AP Road Sector Project, supported by the World Bank, concerns the repair of
850 km of major district roads and State highways

secs.t: Socio-Economic Survey data — prices and inflation

x: CPI-IW inflation was 1.86% in Andhra Pradesh and 2.82% in India during April–October 2025.
The new CPI-AL series introduced from June 2025 uses
as its base.
Andhra Pradesh recorded retail inflation of 4.9%, compared with the national rate of 3.9%, a difference of
1.0 percentage point

secs.t: Socio-Economic Survey data — social indicators, AP vs India

x: Polavaram had the highest sex ratio at 1,051, while Markapuram had the lowest at 962.
The adult sex ratio was 997 and the child sex ratio was 944; both were stated to be above the corresponding Indian figures.
Both statements are true, and the cited MMR and IMR values directly establish why Andhra Pradesh's indicators are lower than India's.

secs.t: Largest, highest and district rankings

x: Andhra Pradesh was ranked
17th
in the NITI Aayog Fiscal Health Index for 2023-24, so 1st, 4th and 28th are wrong.
Visakhapatnam
led in urbanisation at 89.69%, density at 1,870 persons per square kilometre, and literacy at 79.05%.
Polavaram had the lowest urbanisation at 2.84% and density at 54 persons per square kilometre, while Alluri Sitharama Raju had the lowest literacy at 44.67%.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The cited criticism centred on debt of about 36% of GSDP, heavy guarantees and off-budget loans.
The Socio-Economic Survey was skipped during the 2026 Budget session.
Telangana's 2026-27 Budget was ₹3.24 lakh crore, while Andhra Pradesh's was ₹3.32 lakh crore.
The Centre's fiscal-deficit target for 2026-27 was
4.3% of GDP
The 16th Finance Commission found 9% of pension beneficiaries to be ineligible.

rows.title: Andhra Pradesh - projects, investments, MoUs, industrial and infrastructure developments
sub: Group-II S4-18: Andhra Pradesh - projects, MoUs, investments and infrastructure developments

secs.t: Investment summits, SIPB approvals and MoUs → venue and outcome

x: The 30th CII Partnership Summit held at Visakhapatnam in November 2025 resulted in 610 MoUs, investments of ₹13.25 lakh crore and approximately 16 lakh jobs.
APEX Korea is located at
Busan
, South Korea, and functions as Andhra Pradesh’s first overseas investment facilitation centre through APEDB.
Through APEX Korea, Korean firms were invited to participate in the ₹30,000-crore
Dugarajapatnam shipbuilding cluster

secs.t: Industrial corridors, hubs and investors → location — Corridors and hubs

x: VCIC has nodes at Visakhapatnam, Chittoor and Kopparthy over 33,000 acres.
The Kopparthy mega industrial hub is in YSR Kadapa district and covers 3,155 acres.
Orvakal is an HBIC node covering 2,621 acres and includes a 600-acre Drone City.
The Krishnapatnam node of CBIC is in SPSR Nellore and covers 13,919.67 acres.

secs.t: Industrial corridors, hubs and investors → location — Investor → place

x: The respective investments included Reliance’s ₹1,08,010-crore data centre, Reliance’s ₹51,300-crore solar-storage project, Adani’s ₹12,297-crore Kadapa project and Yamanko’s ₹9,398-crore Tirupati project.
Geomysore Services is associated with the first private-sector primary gold mine at Jonnagiri in Kurnool district.
Sagar Defence Engineering
is associated with the world's first autonomous maritime shipbuilding centre at Juvvaladinne in Nellore.

secs.t: Energy projects → district and capacity — Renewables, storage and green hydrogen

x: The Tata Renewable Energy hybrid project has a total capacity of 800 MW:
400 MW solar at Pathikonda and 400 MW wind at Kanekallu
, with an investment of ₹5,750 crore.
The DBFOO thermal project consists of two 800-MW units, giving a total capacity of 1,600 MW, with an estimated cost of up to ₹25,000 crore.

secs.t: Energy projects → district and capacity — Energy data

x: The RDSS was launched in 2021 with an indicated outlay of
₹3.03 lakh crore
Renewable-energy projects totalling 112.45 GW were allocated in June 2026.
Andhra Pradesh had
4.11 lakh
PM Surya Ghar rooftop systems in August 2026 and was among the top four states.
The committee, chaired by the Chief Secretary, cleared ₹522 crore of loss-reduction works for
Godavari Pushkaralu 2027

secs.t: Digital infrastructure → company, place and scale

x: Google's 1-GW AI data centre at Tarluvada (Visakhapatnam) is part of a $15 bn (about Rs 1.35 lakh crore) investment, with Adani and Airtel Nxtra.
The Google AI hub is described as the largest outside the USA, includes a data centre and subsea-cable landing station, and covers 160 acres at Adavivaram–Mudasarlova.

secs.t: Roads, railways and Amaravati → projects and facts — National highways

x: The
Buttaigudem–Kovvur
project involves two-laning over 45 km at a cost of ₹840 crore.
The five-kilometre four-lane road connects Kakinada deep-sea port with NH-216.
The Prime Minister launched projects worth ₹17,900 crore at
Bhogapuram
on 1 August 2026.
The July 2023 Tirupati event included the Thamminapatnam–Narikellapalle project and the Krishnapatnam Port link among three National Highway projects.

secs.t: Roads, railways and Amaravati → projects and facts — South Coast Railway (SCoR)

x: SCoR, promised in the AP Reorganisation Act 2014, began working from 1 June 2026 as India's
18th railway zone
with HQ at Visakhapatnam.
The Visakhapatnam metro proposal has four corridors, 76.70 km and an estimated cost of about ₹28,000 crore; Vijayawada metro projects were also approved by the Governor in January 2026.

secs.t: Ports, fishing harbours and airports → district and status

x: Kakinada Gateway Port is located at Kona in the Kakinada SEZ, has a capacity of 16 MMTPA and is expected to be commissioned in early 2027.
All four statements correctly describe the airport's developer, delivery model, replacement of the INS Dega civil enclave and greenfield status.
Juvvaladinne is in Nellore, Nizampatnam in Bapatla, Machilipatnam in Krishna and Uppada in Kakinada.

secs.t: Irrigation and river-linking projects → river, legal basis and status

x: Polavaram is a national project on the Godavari; completion is targeted for March 2027 (latest target, reaffirmed by the CM in Jul and Sep 2026; the original deadline was Dec 2027) and ₹6,105 crore was provided in the 2026–27 Budget.
In September 2026, Godavari water was sent to North Coastal Andhra through the Left Main Canal using pumps, even though the dam itself remained unfinished.

secs.t: Medical colleges and central institutions → location

x: Markapuram is one of the Phase-I PPP medical colleges, along with Madanapalle, Pulivendula and Adoni.
Ten Critical Care Blocks and twelve Integrated Public Health Laboratories were opened on 12 September 2026 under PM-ABHIM.
The programme involved 17 new government medical colleges, at least 10 of them through PPP, with VGF of about ₹1,468 crore.
AIIMS is at Mangalagiri, IIT at Tirupati, NIT at Tadepalligudem and IIM at Visakhapatnam.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Google stated that it would use air cooling; water use nevertheless remained part of the public debate.

The first Quantum Valley is associated with Amaravati; the first commercial green ammonia plant with Kakinada; the first private-sector primary gold mine with Jonnagiri; and AP's first overseas facilitation centre with Busan.
The PPP mode for government medical colleges was opposed by YSRCP and Praja Arogya Vedika.

rows.title: Andhra Pradesh - awards, GI tags, cultural events, sports and persons in news
sub: Group-II S4-19: Andhra Pradesh - appointments, awards, GI tags and persons in news
Group-II S4-20: Andhra Pradesh - culture, sports, festivals and events

secs.t: State symbols → residual AP vs Telangana

x: The symbols of residual Andhra Pradesh are the Rose-ringed Parakeet, Jasmine, Neem and Blackbuck.
The Telangana animal symbol is Jinka, meaning deer, not Indian Roller.
Red Sanders is endemic to the Seshachalam region, but Neem is the state tree of residual Andhra Pradesh.

secs.t: Padma and national awards → AP recipient and field

x: Exam angle: "which awardee is from AP" - the distractors come from Telangana.
Dr. Nori Dattatreyudu
, a native of Mantada in Krishna district, received the Padma Bhushan for his work as an Indian-American radiation oncologist.
Murali Mohan and Rajendra Prasad, both associated with cinema, were
Padma Shri
awardees in 2026.

secs.t: State honours → Ugadi awards, Nandi and other awardees

x: D. Sivamma is associated with leather puppetry, or Tholu Bommalata, and received the Shilp Guru 2023 honour.
The Nandi Awards and Nandi Natakotsavams are being revived through the Andhra Pradesh Film Development Corporation (
APFDC
The Raghupathi Venkaiah Award is the Nandi
lifetime honour for Telugu cinema
The CM gave
38 Kala Ratna and 122 Ugadi awards

secs.t: Books → authors: Sahitya Akademi and Jnanpith

x: Surada Prasad
received the Sahitya Akademi Yuva Puraskar 2025 and was described as the first fisherman's son to win it.
Viswanatha Satyanarayana, C. Narayana Reddy and Ravuri Bharadwaja are Telugu Jnanpith winners.
Viswanatha Satyanarayana
of Vijayawada was a literary figure, a Jnanpith awardee and the author associated with Ramayana Kalpavruksham.

secs.t: Art forms → meaning, community and records

x: Dhimsa is performed by the Bagata, Valmiki, Konda Dora and Gadaba communities.
The origin of Dhimsa is traced to
Koraput
The revival plan included Tholu Bommalata, Harikatha, Burrakatha, Padya Natakam and the Nandi Natakotsavams.
The Dhimsa Guinness record involving more than 13,000 tribal women was achieved at the new Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport at Bhogapuram.

secs.t: GI tags and ODOP → product, district and category

x: Udayagiri wooden cutlery and Paturu cotton silk sarees are associated with Nellore, while Etikoppaka toys and Payakaraopeta silk sarees are associated with Anakapalli.
Allagadda stone carving is associated with Nandyal, Srikalahasti Kalamkari with Tirupati, Mangalagiri sarees with Guntur and Narasapuram crochet lace with West Godavari.
The central Craft Wood Bank was opened at
Dowleswaram
, along with six other banks including those at Kondapalli, Etikoppaka, Udayagiri and Bobbili.

secs.t: Festivals and utsavs → venue and date

x: Visakha Utsav is linked with Visakhapatnam; Flamingo Festival with Sullurpeta/Nelapattu; Gandikota Festival with Jammalamadugu; and Kondapalli Toys Festival with Kondapalli, NTR.
Telugu Mahotsavam was made annual, Molla Jayanti and the Modakondamma festival were declared State festivals, and Gouthu Latchanna's birth anniversary is observed on 16 August as a State festival.

secs.t: Tableaux and events hosted in AP → city and date

x: The APIIC tableau won the first prize at Tirupati, while the Srisailam temple tableau titled ‘Dharmapatha’ won the second prize at Nandyal.
The 2026 Republic Day tableaux were presented on the theme ‘
150 years of Vande Mataram
The third International Fleet Review was held at Visakhapatnam on 18 February 2026, 71 warships were reviewed from INS Sumedha, and the theme was 'United through Oceans'.

secs.t: Sportspersons from AP → discipline, medal and 2025-26 news

x: Exam angle: match athlete to sport and event. "First Indian woman Olympic medallist" is a regular question.
Jyothi Yarraji returned after a year-long injury, was selected for the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games squad and competes in the 100 m hurdles.
Valluri Ajaya Babu won the
silver
medal in the 79 kg weightlifting category at the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games.
Karnam Malleswari
of Srikakulam won weightlifting bronze (69 kg) at Sydney 2000, the first Olympic medal by an Indian woman and still AP's only Olympic medal.

secs.t: Sports administration, policy and venues

x: A. Ravi Naidu is SAAP Chairman (a-2), S. Bharani is SAAP VC & MD (b-3), and Mandipalli Ramprasad Reddy is the Sports Minister (c-1).
The SAAP Integrated Sports Complex is located at Kommadi in Visakhapatnam and extends over 27 acres with multi-sport academies.
SAAP decided to seek government action to register, recognise and regulate sports associations under the
Sports Act

secs.t: Persons in news → achievement or office

x: Potluri Bhaskara Rao
is the president of the AP Chambers of Commerce and Industry Federation.
Twenty-one children with special needs reached
Everest Base Camp
at an altitude of 5,364 metres in April 2026 under Samagra Shiksha.
Lok Bhavan is the renamed Raj Bhavan, Ashok Gajapathi Raju is Governor of Goa, and Polavaram district (first Collector K. Dinesh Kumar) has its HQ at Rampachodavaram.

secs.t: Appointments and ministers → post and portfolio

x: Exam angle: "who holds X as of <date>". Pawan Kalyan's portfolio has been asked before.

Ponguru Narayana holds Municipal Administration and Urban Development; K. Atchannaidu holds Agriculture and Fisheries; Nimmala Ramanaidu holds Water Resources; and Kandula Durgesh holds Tourism, Culture and Cinematography.
G. Satya Prabhakar Rao became
Additional District & Sessions Judge, Chittoor
in 2022 (PYQ).

secs.t: District and institutional awards and records → AP winner

x: Murugummi, Marella and Thangella
villages of Prakasam district received national Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari awards.
IIITDM Kurnool
was ranked first under the DoT initiative for 100 5G Use Case Labs during January–June 2026.
Alluri Sitharama Raju (ASR) district ranked 1st in India in Basic Infrastructure under the ADP (Mar 2026).

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Jyothi Yarraji and Satwik

of cities met the WHO PM2.5 guideline of 5 µg/m³.

secs.t: Multi-sport games → host, year, India's tally (Olympics, CWG, Asian Games) — Olympic Games

x: Ski mountaineering
, also called skimo, made its Olympic debut at the 2026 Winter Olympics.
Norway
topped the 2026 Winter Olympics medal table with 18 gold medals and 41 medals in total, followed by the USA and the Netherlands.
Asian Games 2026 boxing medallists will go directly to
the 2027 World Championships
, which serve as the first qualifier for LA 2028.

secs.t: Multi-sport games → host, year, India's tally (Olympics, CWG, Asian Games) — Commonwealth Games

x: Commonwealth Sport is headquartered in London (Glasgow hosted the 2026 Games).
Gulveer Singh
was India’s only double medallist at the 2026 Commonwealth Games, winning silver and bronze.
Harsh Singh and Asmita Dey won India’s first Commonwealth Games judo gold medals.
Mirabai Chanu won her third consecutive Commonwealth Games gold medal, becoming the first woman weightlifter to do so.
Ahmedabad
will host the 2030 centenary Commonwealth Games.

secs.t: Multi-sport games → host, year, India's tally (Olympics, CWG, Asian Games) — Asian Games and Asian events

x: The
Satwik–Chirag
men’s doubles pair won gold at the 2023 Asian Games, which India will seek to defend in 2026.
Veer Bhadu
won a bronze medal and became India’s first MMA medallist at the 3rd Asian Youth Games 2025.
Aichi-Nagoya, Japan
hosts the 2026 Asian Games, starting 19 September 2026.

secs.t: Cricket → tournament, winner, venue — ICC World Cups

x: Exam angle: "co-host of the 2025 Women's ODI World Cup" (India, Sri Lanka) and "venue of the 2025 IBA Women's Worlds" (Nis) were both asked in 2025.
India
won its maiden Women's ODI World Cup title by defeating South Africa in November 2025.
Australia won the Women's T20 World Cup, India won the U-19 title and Hockey Asia Cup, and the Indian women finished fifth at the 2026 FIH Hockey World Cup.

secs.t: Cricket → tournament, winner, venue — Domestic leagues and trophies

x: The IPL 2026 final was held on 31 May 2026 at the Narendra Modi Stadium in Ahmedabad.
Royal Challengers Bengaluru defeated Gujarat Titans and secured its second successive IPL title.
Jammu and Kashmir won its first Ranji Trophy title, and the final was its first in approximately 70 years; therefore all three statements are correct.
Harmanpreet Kaur
became the first cricketer to appear in 200 T20Is.

secs.t: Football, hockey and kabaddi → winner, final, title count

x: Spain
defeated Argentina 1-0 after extra time to win the FIFA World Cup 2026.
Mbappé won the Golden Boot with 10 goals and became the all-time leading World Cup scorer with 22 goals.
East Bengal
defeated Mohun Bagan 4-1 to win the 135th Durand Cup, its first Durand title in 22 years.
Services
defeated Kerala to win the 79th Santosh Trophy, securing its eighth title; Abhishek Pawar was associated with the result.

secs.t: Chess players → titles and FIRSTs — Person → title

x: Javokhir Sindarov (Uzbekistan) won it; Praggnanandhaa's firsts are Norway Chess and the Grand Chess Tour.
R. Vaishali
won the Women's Candidates 2026 and is scheduled to challenge Ju Wenjun of China.
Divya Deshmukh
defeated Koneru Humpy in the all-Indian final of the Women's World Cup 2025.
Nodirbek Abdusattorov
won the Tata Steel Masters 2026, securing his first title in the event.
Koneru Humpy and Arjun Erigaisi won bronze medals at Doha in 2025.
D. Gukesh defeated
Ding Liren
in Singapore in 2024 to become World Champion.

secs.t: Chess players → titles and FIRSTs — Chess Olympiad

x: India won both sections at the 45th Chess Olympiad held in Budapest in 2024.

secs.t: Badminton → championship, winner, Indian titles

x: Satwiksairaj-Chirag Shetty won the China Masters in September 2026 and will defend their Asiad gold at the 2026 Asian Games.

Lakshya Sen won the Australian Open Super 500 in 2025; Satwiksairaj-Chirag won the Singapore Open 2026; Sujeet Kalkal and Abhimanyu Mandwal won Asian Championships gold; and Elena Rybakina won the 2026 US Open women's title.

secs.t: Athletes → sport → title / record — Shooting and boxing

x: Esha Singh won 25m pistol gold at Munich with a world-record qualification score.
Jaismine Lamboria and Minakshi Hooda were gold medallists at the 2025 World Boxing Championships.
Chandrika Pujari won gold at the World Boxing Futures Cup 2026 held in Bangkok.
Niš in Serbia hosted the IBA Women's World Boxing Championships 2025.

secs.t: Athletes → sport → title / record — Athletics, wrestling, para-sports, tennis

x: Gurindervir Singh
recorded 10.09 seconds in the 100m at the Federation Cup 2026, becoming the first Indian to run under 10.10 seconds.
Sawan Barwal recorded 2:11:58 at Rotterdam and broke
Shivnath Singh
's 1978 marathon mark.
Payal Nag became the
world's first quadruple amputee to win an international gold
in para archery at Bangkok.

secs.t: Khelo India Games → host state and new sports

x: Rajasthan hosted the fifth edition, which introduced beach volleyball, canoeing-kayaking and cycling.
The 6th Khelo India Winter Games used Leh for ice events and Gulmarg for snow events.
Bihar
hosted KIYG 2025 (in the APPSC 2025 key) and later won the 'Best State for Promotion of Sports' award.
Figure skating
debuted at the 6th KIWG (Leh and Gulmarg).

secs.t: Sports schemes, funding and awards → year and outlay

x: The record allocation for the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports was
in the Union Budget 2026–27.
The 2025 awards included 17 Arjuna Awards and five Dronacharya Awards, including boxing coach Chhote Lal Yadav, while no Khel Ratna was awarded.
The Rashtriya Khel Protsahan Puraskar went to the
Army Paralympic Node, Pune

secs.t: Hosting rights, venues and AP infrastructure → place

x: New Delhi
hosted the 2025 World Para Athletics Championships, marking India’s first time hosting the event.
India hosted the first Kho Kho World Cup in
New Delhi
from 13 to 19 January 2025, with 23 countries participating.
The 2030 Commonwealth Games are assigned to Ahmedabad; the 2026 FIH Hockey World Cups to the Netherlands and Belgium; the 2026 Olympiad to Samarkand; and the 2026 World Championship match to Geneva.

secs.t: Records and FIRSTs → quick revision

x: Praggnanandhaa was the first Indian to win Norway Chess, Divya Deshmukh won the Women's World Cup 2025, Mirabai Chanu won a 3rd straight CWG gold (2026), and India hosted the World Para Athletics Championships for the first time in 2025 (New Delhi).
Payal Nag became the
first quadruple amputee to win an international gold medal
, making it one of India's sporting firsts of 2025-26.

x: Koneru Humpy and Jyothi Yarraji
are identified as being from Andhra Pradesh in the stated sports context.
Ahmedabad's association with the 2030 Commonwealth Games and New Delhi's hosting of the 2026 BWF World Championships support India's 2036 Olympic bid.
C is wrong: the 2026 Asian Games were held at Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, not in India, and India had hosted the Asian Games long before (New Delhi, 1951 and 1982).

secs.t: National days → date → person or event commemorated

x: Exam angle: APPSC 2025 asked Consumer Day (24 Dec) and the new fixed date of Ayurveda Day (23 Sep).
Good Governance Day is observed on 25 December, the birth anniversary of former Prime Minister
Atal Bihari Vajpayee
National Space Day, observed on 23 August, commemorates Chandrayaan-3’s Vikram landing at Shiv Shakti Point in 2023.

Anti-Terrorism Day (21 May) marks Rajiv Gandhi's assassination in 1991; National Handloom Day (7 August) marks the launch of the Swadeshi Movement in 1905; National Sports Day (29 August) is Dhyan Chand's birth anniversary; Hindi Diwas (14 September) marks the 1949 adoption of Hindi as official language.
The theme of the 2nd National Space Day in 2025 was '
Aryabhatta to Gaganyaan: Ancient Wisdom to Infinite Possibilities
Rashtriya Ekta Diwas
is observed on 31 October in memory of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel; 2025 marked his 150th birth anniversary.

secs.t: Days → who declared, which date, first year

x: India proposed the observance, the UNGA adopted it in 2014 through Resolution 69/131, and 21 June is the summer solstice in the Northern Hemisphere.
Ayurveda Day was fixed as
23 September
from 2025, corresponding to the autumnal equinox.
Samvidhan Hatya Diwas is observed on 25 June to mark the 1975 Emergency.
Sports Day began in 1995, Constitution Day in 2015, Clean Air Day in 2020 and National Space Day in 2024.

secs.t: UN days, years and decades → date and theme — UN and international days

x: International Women’s Day is 8 March, World Earth Day is 22 April, World Oceans Day is 8 June, and World Youth Skills Day is 15 July.
The 2026 theme of World Zoonoses Day is “
One World, One Health: Prevent Zoonoses
The 2025 theme of the International Day of Sign Languages, observed on 23 September, was “
No Human Rights Without Sign Language Rights
India observes the day as
Swachh Vayu Diwas
, when the Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan awards are given.
International Labour Day was declared by the International Socialist Congress at
Paris in 1889
The 2026 International Labour Day theme concerns
healthy psychosocial workplaces and mental well-being
, under the ILO association.
The 2024 theme was '
Learning for lasting peace
' (in the APPSC 2024 and 2025 keys).

secs.t: UN days, years and decades → date and theme — International years and decades

x: India marked the 2025 International Year of Quantum Science and Technology through the
Amaravati Quantum Valley

secs.t: Anniversaries → person or event → year

x: The 150th anniversary of Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay's
Vande Mataram
was associated with the theme of the Republic Day celebrations of 2026.
Sardar Patel's 150th birth anniversary fell on 31 October 2025; Bhupen Hazarika's birth centenary was observed in 2025; and a centenary stamp for Satish Gujral was issued in August 2026.
The Coast Guard golden jubilee is scheduled for 2027, the 5th Coast Guard Global Summit is to be hosted by India at Chennai, and Indian hockey completed 100 years in November 2025.

secs.t: Books → authors and literary awards — Autobiographies, memoirs and AP books

x: 'Triumph of the Indian Republic: My Life, My Struggles' is the autobiography of former President
Ram Nath Kovind
, who served as the 14th President of India from 2017 to 2022.

'The Library Man of India' is by P.P. Sathyan; 'A Walk Up the Hill' (2023) is by Madhav Gadgil; '281 and Beyond' is V.V.S. Laxman's autobiography; 'Neither Roses Nor Thorns' is by Justice H.R. Khanna, recalling his ADM Jabalpur dissent.

'Ajeyudu' by T.D. Prasad is on CM N. Chandrababu Naidu. 'Art of Andhra Pradesh' is by Kalasagar Yellapu ('Prime Ministers of India' is Dasari Alwar Swamy's), 'Gurajada Annarasha' studies Gurajada Apparao's style, and 'The Library Man of India' is on P.N. Panicker.

secs.t: Books → authors and literary awards — Award-winning books → author

x: 'Taiwan Travelogue' was written by
Yang Shuang-zi
and translated by Lin King.
The first Jnanpith Award was given in 1965 to G. Sankara Kurup, not R. Vairamuthu.
Crimson Spring was written by Navtej Sarna, Jeete Jee Allahabad by Mamta Kalia, Maayaamanushyar by N. Prabhakaran and Flesh by David Szalay.

secs.t: Literary festivals and book fairs → venue and guests

x: Minister
Kollu Ravindra
was the chief guest at the 36th Vijayawada Book Festival, which ended on 12 January 2026.
The Visakha Book Festival was held at the
Andhra University Grounds
in January 2026.
The Hindu Lit For Life 2026 took place at Lady Andal School, Chennai, on 17–18 January, with the three named speakers among its participants.

secs.t: Observance days → chronology (revision)

x: National Youth Day is on 12 January, Girl Child Day on 24 January, Voters' Day on 25 January and Environment Day on 5 June.

The correct sequence is Library Day on 12 August, Space Day on 23 August, Sports Day on 29 August, Teachers' Day on 5 September, Literacy Day on 8 September, Hindi Diwas on 14 September and Ayurveda Day on 23 September.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Ajeyudu and Gurajada Annarasha
were identified as Andhra Pradesh-related books in the 2026 current-affairs events.
Andhra Pradesh observes Yoga Day, Youth Day and the Day against Drug Abuse in all districts.
The Booker Prize concerns original English fiction, whereas the International Booker recognises fiction translated into English and shares the £50,000 prize between the author and translator.

secs.t: Heads of international organisations → person

Khalilur Rahman of Bangladesh
won the post, defeating Cyprus.
Bimal N. Patel was elected to ITLOS (Hamburg; 21 judges) for a 9-year term, 2026-2035.
India won its 7th UNHRC term (2026-28) unopposed, and about 100 APNRTS Goodwill Ambassadors were posted in the six Gulf countries in 2026.

secs.t: Posts in India → holder

x: The CEC and Election Commissioners hold office for six years or until age 65, whichever is earlier.
Mallikarjun Kharge was reappointed
Leader of Opposition in the Rajya Sabha
in June 2026.
T.V. Somanathan
is the Cabinet Secretary (a PYQ fact) and got a one-year extension from the ACC in August 2026.

secs.t: Appointment rules → term, appointing authority, Article

x: A candidate needs at least 9 ‘Encourage’ votes out of 15 and must receive no ‘Discourage’ vote from any permanent member.
The Cabinet Secretary is appointed by the ACC, has a two-year term extendable to four years, ranks 11th and heads the NCMC.
The temporary inclusion of the Chief Justice of India arose from the Anoop Baranwal decision of March 2023, as clarified by the Supreme Court in May 2026.

secs.t: Record-setting FIRSTs and influence lists → person

x: Narendra Modi
became India’s longest-serving elected Prime Minister through the Cabinet resolution dated 10 June 2026.
Kranti Gaud, with a five-wicket haul, and Yastika Bhatia, with a score of 113, became the first women on the Lord’s honours board.
Bobby Mukkamala became the first person of Indian heritage to head the American Medical Association in June 2025.

x: All four pairs are correctly matched.
Alan Greenspan was the former Chairman of the U.S. Federal Reserve, not the former President of the World Bank.
Mudragada Padmanabham’s family declined State honours.
Girish Bharadwaj
was popularly known as the “Bridge Man of India.”.

Alla Nani was a former AP Deputy CM (died Sep 2026), C.D. Gopinath was India's oldest Test cricketer, Subhash Kashyap was a former Lok Sabha Secretary-General, and B.C. Khanduri was a former Union Highways Minister.
